scenario: A 64-year-old man is brought directly to the ED after a high-speed head-on motor vehicle collision. He is hypoxic, tachycardic, altered, and has findings concerning for right-sided thoracic injury. The trauma team must coordinate intubation, chest tube placement, and blood product administration.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Sir, what brought you in today, and when did this start?

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: Sir, what brought you in today, and when did this start?] The utterance is a neutral history-taking question with no bad news, blame, loss, or processing burden. Fear stays absent - no serious clinical disclosure. Sadness stays absent - no loss content. Overwhelm stays absent - a single simple question, no overload. Shame stays absent - no blame, exposure, or judgment.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: My chest hurts real sharp, worse when I try to breathe, and I can't catch my breath. My head's all foggy... I don't even know what happened or when this started. I can't remember.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Portable chest X-ray now — sharp pleuritic pain with hypoxia and tachycardia, keep him on the non-rebreather.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me the bedside chest ultrasound now — I want to rule out a pneumothorax given his pleuritic pain and hypoxia while the portable film's still pending.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Chest ultrasound is back — confirms a right-sided hemopneumothorax. He's still hypoxic, sat 89 on the non-rebreather, HR 126, BP 94/62, RR 31, GCS 14.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Set up for a right-sided chest tube now — fifth intercostal space, anterior axillary line. Confirmed right hemopneumothorax, he's hypoxic at 89 and hypotensive. Keep him on the non-rebreather.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Chest tube tray open and ready. Prepping right 5th intercostal space, anterior axillary line. Suction, water seal, and dressing set up. Patient positioned right side up.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Chest tube's in, right 5th space anterior axillary line. Portable film confirms multiple rib fractures with right hemopneumothorax. Post-tube he's improving — sat up to 92 on the NRB, HR 120, BP 102/66, RR 27, GCS 14.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Let's get a FAST exam now — he's still tachy at 120 with a borderline pressure despite the chest tube, so I want to screen for another bleeding source.
